questions.q: What is the time complexity of random access by index (e.g. prices[5]) on a std::vector?
options: O(n)
O(log n)
O(n log n)
questions.explain: std::vector stores its elements contiguously, so indexing into it is a direct, constant-time offset calculation.

questions.q: What distinguishes std::array<T, N> from std::vector<T>?
options: std::array can grow and shrink at runtime, std::vector cannot
std::array's size N is a compile-time constant with no heap allocation; std::vector is dynamically resizable on the heap
std::array can only hold integers
std::vector is faster for every operation than std::array
questions.explain: std::array is a fixed-size, stack-allocated array whose size is fixed at compile time, while std::vector dynamically allocates and can resize at runtime.

questions.q: Why would you choose std::deque over std::vector for a given use case?
options: deque offers faster random access than vector
deque needs to efficiently insert and remove elements at both the front and the back
deque uses less memory than vector in all cases
deque guarantees sorted order of its elements
questions.explain: std::deque supports O(1) push_front and push_back, unlike std::vector where push_front is O(n) because every existing element must shift.

questions.q: What ordering guarantee does iterating over a std::map<std::string, double> provide?
options: No guarantee — order is effectively random
Elements are visited in insertion order
Elements are visited in sorted order by key
Elements are visited in reverse insertion order
questions.explain: std::map is backed by a balanced binary tree ordered by key, so iteration always visits entries in sorted key order.

questions.q: Why does std::unordered_map typically outperform std::map for pure lookups when sorted order isn't needed?
options: unordered_map stores elements contiguously like vector
unordered_map uses hashing for average O(1) lookup, versus map's O(log n) tree-based lookup
unordered_map is a newer container, so it's always faster
map cannot perform lookups at all
questions.explain: unordered_map hashes keys for average constant-time operations, while map's balanced-tree structure gives logarithmic-time operations but preserves sorted order.
